message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules** | # | Rule | Details | |---|------|---------| | 1 | **Objective** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are earned by collecting cards left in opponents’ hands when you go out. | | 2 | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | 3 | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | 4 | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card from your hand that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top card on the discard pile. | | 5 | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn (must be challenged if you suspect it was illegally played). | | 6 | **Drawing** | If you cannot play a card, draw one from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | 7 | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have only one card left, shout “UNO!” before your next opponent takes a turn. If you fail to call UNO and another player catches you, you must draw two cards as a penalty. | | 8 | **Winning a Round** | You win a round when you discard all your cards. | | 9 | **Scoring** | • Number cards: face value.
• Draw Two, Reverse, Skip: 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four: 50 points each.
Points from the cards remaining in opponents’ hands are added to the winner’s score. | |10 | **Game End** | The game ends when a player reaches the target score (usually 500). | --- ### Quick Play Variations | Variation | How It Works | |-----------|--------------| | **House Rules** | Many groups add house rules (e.g., “Stacking” where +2 cards can be stacked, “Seven-O” where 7s reverse direction and 0s reset the pile). | | **Uno Attack** | Uses a special card‑shuffling machine that can randomly deal extra cards to players. | | **Uno Flip** | Adds a “Flip” card that flips the deck to a new side with different colors and higher‑value special cards. | --- ### Tips for Beginners 1. **Keep track of colors** – Try to hold onto cards of the same color to reduce the chance of drawing later. 2. **Use wild cards strategically** – Save them for when you’re stuck or when you want to change the color to suit your hand. 3. **Watch opponents** – Notice which colors they’re avoiding; this can hint at what they’re holding. 4. **Practice “UNO” timing** – Call UNO right after you play your second‑to‑last card, not just before you go out. Enjoy playing Uno!
